text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 3x nodes in us-west-2 serving-runtime pool reporting OOM kills + CUDA driver errors. Auto-retry on requests failing with STATUS 13. Triggered at 08:12 UTC. Pager escalated to #eng-oncall. :rotating_light:
jenna_oncall: ack — looking. Which allocator is showing the slow memory growth?
liam_runtime: kv-cache/paged-attention allocator. We've seen steady resident growth over ~36h on these hosts, then paging spikes and container restarts.
amanda_ops: confirming increased eviction counts in metrics; per-node mem_use rises ~2-3%/hr.
diego_infra: logs show repeated: "cudaDriverGetVersion failed: unknown error" and then kernel OOM killing process pid=4123 (serving-runtime). Full snippet: ```kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4123 (serving-runtime) total-vm:1123456kB, anon-rss:1048576kB```.
liam_runtime: here's the runtime log around the crash: ```E[serving] kv_cache: fragment_count=4872, slab_frag=0.73, live_pages=22940, reclaimed=12
E[alloc] paged_attn: alloc failed, requested=8192, available_page_list=0
E[cuda] cuCtxCreate: error 0x7f```.
jenna_oncall: immediate mitigations: (1) drain the three affected nodes, (2) enable aggressive kv eviction feature-flag for the pool, (3) scale up replacement nodes in another az. I'll run cordon/drain now.
amanda_ops: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for node-17, then node-22, node-19.
ops-bot: Started new replacement instances (mGPU-pool) in us-west-2a, target 3 nodes.
liam_runtime: quick hotfix we can flip: set KV_EVICTION_WARMUP=0.6 (was 0.9) and KV_RECLAIM_BATCH=128 to force earlier eviction and higher reclaim throughput. This should reduce live_pages pressure.
diego_infra: applied runtime-config change to serving-runtime configmap on the pool; rolling restart in progress: `kubectl rollout restart ds/serving-runtime -n inference`.
cs_beth: CS note — some customers in us-west-2 are seeing ~5-10% increase in 5xxs on text-generation endpoints since 08:10 UTC. Most are transient but a few long-running chat sessions got truncated. 
jenna_oncall: counted failed requests ~2.1k in the last 20m; error spikes line up with node restarts. Marking customer-impact = partial-degradation.
liam_runtime: added temporary guard in routing: route requests with seq_length > 1024 away from the pool while we stabilize (canary to lower-capacity variants). This reduces large KV growth.
amanda_ops: node drain complete for 3 nodes. Replacement nodes healthy. Memory graphs flattening — growth rate dropped to ~0.2%/hr after eviction flag.
liam_runtime: we should capture a heap/kv-snapshot from one of the affected instances before full restart completes — grabs insights on fragmentation pattern. I'll `kubectl exec -it` into a pod and trigger `serving-runtime dump-kv --json > /tmp/kv-dump.json` now.
diego_infra: FYI kernel oops pattern also showed a memory compaction failure on 2 nodes — might be low host-level reserved memory (cgroup limits + GPU driver). Filing infra ticket to audit host tuning.
cs_beth: passing a short status to customers: "We've mitigated a serving disruption in us-west-2 affecting a small fraction of requests; mitigation steps applied and traffic being routed away from unstable nodes. We'll follow up once we confirm stability."
jenna_oncall: summary for handoff -> next oncall: incident started 08:12 UTC, cause: slow kv/paged-attention memory creep leading to fragmentation and paging, precipitating OOMs + CUDA driver errors. Actions taken: cordoned/drained 3 nodes, rolled config to force earlier KV eviction, rolled serving-runtime DS, applied routing rule to avoid long sequences. Current status: replacement nodes healthy, error rate dropping but not fully back to baseline. Postmortem action items: 1) implement finer-grained KV eviction metrics & alerts (liam), 2) host tuning for compaction and driver stability (diego), 3) add early-warning predictive regression for slab_frag > 0.65 (jenna).
liam_runtime: attaching the kv-dump filename on the node: `/var/tmp/kv-dump-1955012345.json` — will upload to the incident bucket. Also put a short repro script in the ticket to reproduce steady kv growth (stress with many long sequences + repeated prefix caching).
diego_infra: infra ticket #INF-1198 created for host compaction audit and driver upgrade window.
jenna_oncall: handing off to amanda_ops for overnight watch. Please keep routing rule in place for another 2h and verify that reclaimed pages stays >500/s and slab_frag reduces under 0.6 before removing.
amanda_ops: ack, will monitor and escalate if residual node flaps. Leaving a note: if we see `cuCtxCreate` errors returning frequently again, flip traffic to us-east-1 DR pool.
cs_beth: I'll send customers a follow-up in 2 hours with our mitigation summary and ask CS to collect any truncated session IDs for QA.
jenna_oncall: thanks everyone — marking incident as "mitigated, monitoring". Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
